steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.

title: FactorEngram: Factorized N-gram Memory with Basis-Level Gating for Language Models
summary: The method replaces monolithic hashed n-gram embedding lookups (as in Engram) with a shared dictionary of basis vectors, sparsity-regularized coefficients, and per-basis contextual gating scored against the backbone hidden state. It costs additional memory-branch parameters, per-basis scoring computation, and training complexity, and it requires training the backbone jointly with the memory rather than retrofitting an existing model. Adoption can fail because benefits are demonstrated only on 340M and 1B models trained with the branch in place, insertion depth is sensitive (middle layers before attention were found effective), and hash-table and dictionary sizing introduce new hyperparameters whose gains may not transfer to other scales or workloads.
rationale: The technique requires training a backbone jointly with the memory branch, which is infeasible under the reader's constrained infrastructure, and the abstract offers no quantified gains at a scale the reader could reproduce.
technique: Factorized n-gram memory with basis-level contextual gating
